it-2pam.title: Landscape: dark volcanic rock, yellow lichen, cacti
it-2pam.summary: A volcanic island south-west of Sicily: dark rock walls and houses, yellow lichen on rocks, and lots of cacti.

it-42k5.title: Google car: low camera, long antenna, flag, lake west
it-42k5.summary: A small exclave inside Switzerland shows a low camera with a long antenna and a flag, and a lake to the west. Some Swiss areas have the same antenna.

it-5TiR.title: Landscape: grey rocks sticking out of the ground
it-5TiR.summary: On the western island, especially the north-east, grey rocks poke out of the ground. Sicily has similar rocks but is much drier.

it-6adv.title: Guardrail: double guardrails
it-6adv.summary: Double guardrails, with two rails stacked, are very common.

it-7iSX.title: Sign: blue national road sign, green on highways
it-7iSX.summary: National roads have blue direction signs with a white-and-blue border. Motorways have green signs with a white-and-green border.

it-7zlG.title: Chevron: white arrows on black
it-7zlG.summary: White arrows on a black background. Spain, Greece and Albania use the same in southern Europe.

it-8uch.title: Landscape: tall wide mountain ranges, deep valleys
it-8uch.summary: In the north, tall, wide mountain ranges and deep valleys.

it-9MDD.title: Houses: solid wooden shutters, black hinges
it-9MDD.summary: Solid wooden shutters with black metal hinges are common in the north-east, especially one region.

it-AHSj.title: Sign: road numbers start with SS, SR or SP
it-AHSj.summary: Road numbers usually begin with SS (state), SR (regional) or SP (provincial). The second letter shows the road type.

it-AHUP.title: Landscape: huge volcano in the distance
it-AHUP.summary: Europe's tallest volcano towers over the landscape from far away in eastern Sicily.

it-BBrE.title: Bollard: triangular, black top, red front reflector
it-BBrE.summary: White triangular bollard with a black top, a red reflector at the front and a white one at the back. Albania uses the same one.

it-CcGf.title: Houses: pastel stone, terracotta roofs, split shutters
it-CcGf.summary: Pastel stone houses with terracotta roofs. Wooden shutters are very common and split in two, opening sideways.

it-F3fZ.title: Landscape: dry hills, rocky mountains
it-F3fZ.summary: On the large southern island: arid, hilly farmland, often next to rocky mountains.

it-GY26.title: Road lines: white solid edges, no centre line
it-GY26.summary: Very common: solid white edge lines with no middle line. Less common in other Mediterranean countries.

it-IZSl.title: Language: French on signs, "rue" next to "via"
it-IZSl.summary: In the north-west valley, signs show French as well. Street signs often use both via and rue.

it-K2KL.title: Landscape: volcanic islands, white villas on slopes
it-K2KL.summary: A volcanic archipelago north of Sicily with volcanic soil, stone pines, olive trees and cacti. White tourist villas are common in the hills.

it-KSAH.title: City: canals through most of the city
it-KSAH.summary: Canals run through most of the city, so streets are mostly water.

it-NzGb.title: Pole: round concrete
it-NzGb.summary: Lots of round concrete poles, which most other Mediterranean countries do not have.

it-PYmb.title: Crops: rice in the northern plain
it-PYmb.summary: Rice grows mainly in the western and central part of the Po valley, and less often in Sardinia.

it-Q35Q.title: Landscape: twin volcanoes forming a valley
it-Q35Q.summary: On one of the volcanic islands, two volcanoes form a valley across the island.

it-Qtgc.title: Pole: wooden with small white sticker
it-Qtgc.summary: Wooden poles often carry a small white sticker.

it-RTSX.title: Landscape: farmland on rolling hills, forested valleys
it-RTSX.summary: A Mediterranean look: farm fields on rolling hills and forested mountain valleys.

it-RnwF.title: Sign: black or dark grey backs
it-RnwF.summary: The back of road signs is very often black or dark grey.

it-T4R2.title: Landscape: totally flat and hazy
it-T4R2.summary: A completely flat plain with some of the worst air in Europe, so much of the coverage looks hazy.

it-TXiT.title: Sign: pedestrian sign, 5 stripes, no belt
it-TXiT.summary: Pedestrian sign with five stripes and a basic figure without a belt.

it-TyCh.title: Sign: white street sign, thin blue border
it-TyCh.summary: Street signs are usually white with a thin blue border and black text.

it-UJSC.title: Language: Slovene bilingual signs near the border
it-UJSC.summary: Close to the north-eastern border you find signs in both languages, with Slovene as the second.

it-WLd3.title: Houses: rough unpainted brown-grey bricks
it-WLd3.summary: In and around one central region, many buildings use irregular unpainted brown-grey bricks. North-east Spain has a similar style.

it-ZxGw.title: Language: German bilingual signs in the north
it-ZxGw.summary: One northern region has a German majority, so signs are bilingual in German.

it-a1vN.title: Landscape: mountain ridge splitting a flat island
it-a1vN.summary: Mountains run north to south and split the island in two, with flat areas and rock walls on both sides. Unlike nearby islands it is not volcanic.

it-aA4U.title: Landscape: volcano with white stripe near the top
it-aA4U.summary: A volcano with an almost white stripe of dirt along its upper slope. Easy to spot from afar.

it-aDjA.title: Sign: no-parking sign saying "passo carrabile"
it-aDjA.summary: A no-parking sign with the words passo carrabile (driveway), common in towns. The top usually shows the municipality name.

it-clmq.title: Language: double consonants, many i, vowel endings
it-clmq.summary: Lots of double consonants and many letter i, plus ì, é and à. Most words end in a vowel. Street signs usually say via.

it-dfcb.title: Plants: cacti in the south
it-dfcb.summary: Cacti are most common in the south: Sicily, southern Sardinia and the south of Apulia.

it-dto7.title: Google car: low Gen 4 smallcam, big round blur
it-dto7.summary: A Gen 4 camera mounted lower than normal, with a big round blur at the bottom and a small bump at the front. The blur can be transparent and hard to spot.

it-gSjf.title: Guardrail: end flattens, widens, bends away
it-gSjf.summary: Guardrail ends get flatter and wider and bend away from the road.

it-hAqF.title: Sign: blue direction sign, white arrow, capitals
it-hAqF.summary: Blue direction signs with a white arrow. All letters are capitals.

it-hndZ.title: Houses: pale, flat roofs, 2-3 floors
it-hndZ.summary: In the heel region, very light-coloured houses with flat roofs, two to three floors. Sometimes reminiscent of the Middle East.

it-kMZN.title: Landscape: olive groves, bright rock walls, red soil
it-kMZN.summary: In the south-east heel, many olive plantations with bright rock walls and noticeably red soil. South-east Sicily looks similar.

it-lfUH.title: Flags: every region has its own flag
it-lfUH.summary: Each region has its own unique flag, which helps place you in a region.

it-lm-2245.title: Language: useful words (senso unico, piazza, vietato)
it-lm-2245.summary: Handy words: senso unico (one way), di (of), castello, prezzi (prices), piazza, autostrada (motorway), vietato (forbidden), polizia, sconto (discount).

it-lm-2246.title: Sign: via, strada, viale, tangenziale
it-lm-2246.summary: Street signs mostly say via. Strada also means street and is used on rural roads; viale is avenue and tangenziale is ring road. Romanian uses strada more.

it-lm-2247.title: Language: vowel endings, -zione, gli, gn, sci
it-lm-2247.summary: Most words end in a vowel and double consonants are common. Look for endings -zione, -tà, -aggio, -mento and letter groups gli, gn, sci.

it-lm-2995.title: Sign: blue corners outside the white edge
it-lm-2995.summary: Italy, Romania, Serbia and Slovenia look much alike. Italy shows blue corners outside the white edge, while Romania has no white or silver border.

it-lm-558213.title: Sign: street sign with unusual font, years below
it-lm-558213.summary: One northern city has street signs in a unique font, sometimes with years on the bottom.

it-lm-558217.title: Sign: street sign with logo top left
it-lm-558217.summary: One southern port city has street signs with a unique logo in the top left.

it-lm-558219.title: Sign: street sign with extra name under it
it-lm-558219.summary: One southern city has street signs in a unique font with an extra name under the street name.

it-lm-558220.title: Sign: street sign with 4 dots in each corner
it-lm-558220.summary: One Sicilian city has street signs with four dots in each corner.

it-lm-558221.title: Sign: street sign on 3 small supports
it-lm-558221.summary: One Tuscan city has street signs held by 3 small supports: one on top and two at the bottom.

it-lm-558222.title: Sign: huge street sign, thick frame, roman numerals
it-lm-558222.summary: The capital has the most distinctive street signs: bigger than any other, with a very thick frame and roman numerals in the top right.

it-mzWF.title: Phone numbers: first area-code digit rises east then south
it-mzWF.summary: The first digit of the area code generally increases going east, then south.

it-n7fO.title: Google car: gloomy overcast Gen 2
it-n7fO.summary: This small island has only overcast Gen 2 coverage, which mostly looks gloomy.

it-nLtP.title: Houses: grey uneven bricks, Alpine look
it-nLtP.summary: In the north-west valley, buildings use grey uneven bricks and look Alpine. They can look a bit like Andorran architecture.

it-q7lg.title: Marker: white square, roman numeral over number
it-q7lg.summary: A white square km marker with a roman numeral on top and a regular number below. The number is kilometres; the roman numeral is hundreds of metres.

it-qoV6.title: Guardrail: red front reflectors
it-qoV6.summary: Guardrails have red reflectors on the front. This mainly separates it from Spain, which uses yellow.

it-s1Uh.title: Landscape: volcano to the south or east of a city plain
it-s1Uh.summary: Vesuvius is often seen to the south or east from the plains around Naples.

it-s80c.title: Landscape: small mountain-ringed plain, north-south grid
it-s80c.summary: A small plain surrounded by mountains in central Italy, with roads in a grid running exactly north-south.

it-sYKL.title: Plate: blue strips both sides, short front
it-sYKL.summary: Blue strips on both sides of the plate, and a front plate noticeably shorter than most European ones. Together that is unique. Albania has two strips but long front plates.

differs.how: Two blue strips but front plates are not short
Only a small strip on the right, front not short

it-tpUa.title: Houses: big white stone, wooden details
it-tpUa.summary: In the Alps, large buildings with white stone walls and wooden details.

it-uuBU.title: Pole: concrete trident tops
it-uuBU.summary: The most common pole top is a concrete trident, with a few possible insulator layouts. The two in the picture are the most common.

it-zeHg.title: Plants: citrus plantations in the far south
it-zeHg.summary: Citrus groves are mostly in eastern Sicily and the southern tip of the mainland toe.

it-zq9T.title: Houses: round stone cone roofs (trulli)
it-zq9T.summary: This cone-shaped roof style, a trullo, exists only in one valley in the south-east. It is especially common around one town.
